header.title: Vision Verification
header.description: AI-powered screenshot verification that confirms test results visually.

whatIs.title: What is Vision Verification?
whatIs.description: Vision verification adds a second layer of confidence to your test assertions. When it is enabled, after a standard DOM-based verification passes, the system:
steps: Takes a screenshot of the page
Highlights the verified element with a red bounding box
Sends the screenshot to an AI vision model
Asks: "Is this element actually visible on the page?"
whatIs.catches: This catches cases where an element exists in the DOM but is not truly visible to a user: hidden behind overlays, clipped by overflow, rendered off-screen, or styled with zero opacity.

quickSetup.description: Add the vision block to your endorphin.config.ts:
quickSetup.result: That is all. Vision verification now runs automatically after every verification tool call.

supplement.title: Supplement mode
supplement.description: The DOM verification result is the primary source of truth. The vision result is added as an informational note. Use this mode when you trust DOM verification but want extra confidence.

primary.title: Primary mode
primary.description: The vision result overrides the DOM verification result. Use this mode when DOM verification is unreliable, for example when elements are visually hidden but still present in the DOM.

scenarios.hiddenByCss: Elements hidden by CSS (opacity, visibility, z-index)
scenarios.falsePositives: Debugging false positives from DOM checks

tools.title: Which Tools Support Vision?
tools.description: Vision verification runs automatically on all verification tools:

items.verifyElement: Element visibility and state (exists, visible, enabled, and so on)
items.verifyTextContent: Specific text content appears on the page
items.verifyTitle: Page title matches the expected value
items.verifyListVisible: Multiple items are visible on the page

tools.note: You do not need to change your test instructions. If vision is enabled in your config, it activates automatically whenever the AI agent calls a verification tool.

autoHighlight.title: Auto-Highlight Bounding Boxes
autoHighlight.description: When vision is enabled, a 1px red bounding box is drawn automatically around the verified element before the screenshot is taken. This helps the vision model locate and focus on the correct element.

cssSelectors.title: CSS selectors
cssSelectors.description: From verifyElement. The framework calls highlightElement(), which uses getBoundingClientRect() to position a red border around the matched element.

textContent.title: Text content
textContent.description: From verifyTextContent and verifyListVisible. The framework calls highlightText(), which uses a TreeWalker to find matching text nodes and draws a bounding box around them.

cleanup.title: Cleanup
cleanup.description: Highlights are removed automatically after the screenshot is captured. They never appear in later screenshots or affect your page layout.

mixed.envNote: Make sure the right API key is set in your .env file for each provider you use:

options.maxTokens: Maximum response tokens from the vision model
options.mode: How the vision result is used relative to DOM verification

visualUi.title: Visual UI testing
visualUi.description: Confirming styling, layout, or visibility changes that DOM checks alone cannot catch.

hiddenElements.title: Hidden element detection
hiddenElements.description: Catching elements that exist in the DOM but are covered by overlays, modals, or z-index stacking.

critical.title: Critical assertions
critical.description: Adding a second verification layer for high-priority test steps where false positives are unacceptable.

mysteriousPasses.title: Debugging mysterious passes
mysteriousPasses.description: When a test passes but the page looks wrong, vision verification can expose the discrepancy.

functional.title: Simple functional tests
functional.description: If you only check that a page navigates correctly or an API responds, vision adds overhead without much benefit.

highVolume.title: High-volume test suites
highVolume.description: Running vision on hundreds of assertions adds cost and time. Consider enabling it selectively for critical flows.

nonVisual.title: Non-visual checks
nonVisual.description: Verifying page titles, URLs, or hidden form values does not benefit from screenshot analysis.

cost.title: Cost Considerations
cost.description: Each vision verification check incurs additional AI costs:

supplement.title: Use supplement mode for non-critical tests
supplement.description: It adds confidence without changing test outcomes.

selective.title: Enable vision selectively
selective.description: You do not need it on every test. Focus on critical user flows.

cheaperModel.title: Use a cheaper vision model
cheaperModel.description: gpt-4o-mini and gemini-2.0-flash cost less per token while still providing reliable image analysis.

monitor.title: Monitor costs in reports
monitor.description: The HTML reporter shows token usage per step, including vision checks.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.description: Common problems and how to solve them

notRunning.title: Vision verification not running
notRunning.problem: You enabled vision but the verification results do not include vision notes.

authentication.title: "OPENAI_API_KEY required" or authentication errors
authentication.problem: The vision model cannot authenticate with the AI provider.
authentication.solution: The vision model defaults to gpt-4o, which requires an OpenAI API key. Make sure the correct key is set:

boundingBox.title: Bounding box not visible in the screenshot
boundingBox.problem: The red highlight does not appear around the element.
causes: The element is off-screen (scrolled out of view). The framework scrolls to the element before highlighting, but edge cases can occur with sticky headers or complex layouts.
The element has zero width or height. Elements with display: none or zero dimensions cannot be highlighted.
The element is inside an iframe. Cross-origin iframes may block highlight injection.

visionDisagrees.title: Vision says the element is not visible but the DOM says it is
visionDisagrees.description: This is exactly the scenario vision verification is designed for. The element exists in the DOM but is not actually visible to a user. Common causes:
causes: The element is behind a modal or overlay (z-index stacking)
The element is clipped by overflow: hidden on a parent
The element has opacity: 0 or visibility: hidden
The element is positioned off-screen with negative margins
visionDisagrees.advice: If this is expected behavior, switch to supplement mode so the DOM result takes precedence. If you want to catch these issues, use primary mode.
